before.title: Pending tab: one collapsed row per build (rebuild)
before.detail: Rebuild from current main (the old branch claude/pending-tab-one-collapsed-row-per-build is 3000+ commits behind and only has rename commits; ignore it). In the Build Orchestrator's Pending tab, every pending build is ONE collapsed row: title, status/why it's pending, priority, steps done/total, age. Tap the row to expand it and see steps, notes and actions (queue, edit, archive); tap again to collapse. Collapsed by default, remembers expanded rows per viewer. Same for desktop and phone. Uses asset tokens and framework controls; full API parity (deep link, expand/collapse and actions via REST/MCP/CLI/voice). Tests, help, Shipped features. Land when done.

Started run 1 on mossesx-max- (Opus, Phase 1): axf-pending-tab-one-collapsed-row-per-2--paulie.
Claude account: mossesx-max- (mossesx@gmail.com) (axf-pending-tab-one-collapsed-row-per-2--paulie, shared account login)

Brett (06:55): for the CURRENT skin (the console default), the Pending tab uses the 2-row layout, packed with info, buttons and badges. Row 1: title, priority, status badge, action buttons (queue, land, edit, archive, open PR). Row 2: badges/info: commits behind main, date+time added, date+time built, PR #, steps done/total, account/model, why it's pending. Status badges: pending build, queued, building, built/waiting to merge, merging, landed, clashing, failed, held. ANIMATION: any build that's actively doing something (building, merging, splitting, landing) gets its icon/badge animated (e.g. a spinner or pulse) using the skin's animation tokens (#652); idle states stay still; respects reduced motion. Same badge set reused by the every-grid build so all grids can show it.

Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. [ ] s1 (~8 min) Read the current Pending tab in the Build Orchestrator plugin from main. Map where pending rows are drawn, which data they read (status, why pending, priority, steps, age) and which actions exist (queue, edit, archive). Write the map as a short design note in the build report draft.

It also handles the expanded-set state per viewer: toggle, expand, collapse, collapse all and the storage key. Add unit tests for it.
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Server: store expanded rows per viewer on the plugin data dir (key = viewer/session id). Add REST routes: GET pending/rows (summaries plus each row's expanded flag), POST pending/rows/<id>/expand|collapse|toggle and POST pending/rows/collapse-all.
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Build a PendingRow component on framework controls only (TabGroup is not used; Container/Button/Chip/PriorityTag) with asset tokens. Collapsed by default, it shows one line: title, status chip with why it is pending, PriorityTag, steps done/total and age. It has a tap target with aria-expanded and a data-axf-target row:<build> address.
[ ] s5 (~10 min) Expanded body of PendingRow: step list with done ticks and Fable/Opus badges, notes and What Brett said. It also has an actions toolbar (role=toolbar, aria-label, settings id) with Queue, Edit and Archive wired to the existing orchestrator/pipeline calls. Archive keeps its confirm. Tap the header again to collapse.
[ ] s6 (~10 min) Swap the Pending tab's old list for PendingRow rows. Load the expanded state from the GET route, write it back on toggle, and add a Collapse all button. Remove the old multi-row rendering and its dead CSS.
[ ] s7 (~8 min) Phone layout: the collapsed row wraps to two lines at narrow widths without overlap (title, then chips). The expanded actions stay tappable at tap-target size and use tokens only. Run check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars and check-chrome-assets on the plugin and fix any findings.

[ ] s9 (~10 min) API part 2 (MCP, CLI and voice). Add plugin commands pending-rows (list with state), pending-expand, pending-collapse, pending-toggle and pending-collapse-all. They are read statically from the routes for MCP. Add CLI subcommands in orchestrator.mjs (pending rows|expand|collapse|toggle|collapse-all) and AmberX voice actions. Queue, edit and archive reuse the existing commands; check they are listed.
[ ] s10 (~10 min) Parity test: one script calls REST, MCP command, CLI and voice action for list, expand, collapse and toggle on a fixture build. It asserts all four give the same state. Add server route tests for per-viewer separation (viewer A expanded does not expand for viewer B).

[ ] s12 (~10 min) Shots and UI Review: build the console from the worktree (vite preview with mocked /api/me and hub data). Shoot desktop and phone views of the Pending tab: collapsed, one expanded and the phone expanded view. Submit with review.mjs submit with at least 3 choices (row density / chip layout options as assets under plugins/build-orchestrator/assets/), group 'pending-tab-one-collapsed-row-per-2 - <time>'.
[ ] s13 (~10 min) Run the full checks: plugin tests, check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, check-console-control, plugin-lifecycle check, tracker --check and builds-store verify. Confirm the Shipped features ledger got the feature rows from the build hook. Fix anything red.

Update the THREADS.md row. Push the branch and link it with builds-live.mjs link. Open the PR, saying it waits on UI Review and listing the API parity. Add it to the merge queue to land.

Server: store expanded rows per viewer on the plugin data dir (key = viewer/session id). Add REST routes: GET pending/rows (summaries plus each row's expanded flag), POST pending/rows/<id>/expand|collapse|toggle and POST pending/rows/collapse-all.

before.title: Move build orchestrator to axHub
before.detail: Move the entire build orchestrator (queue, pending, splitter, dispatcher/pipeline tick, reconciler, slots, accounts, builds store, notes, steps, landing) out of the console plugin and into axHub (MossesX/axHub), running on the VPS, so builds are managed whether the console is up or not. Staged so nothing breaks mid-flight: (1) Run AFTER auto-lander-controls-in-the-gate-plugin lands (gate + merge queue already in axHub). Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.

Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.

Build a console plugin 'gate' with tabs: Rules (the checks a build must pass before it lands: CI green, tests, theme/controls checks, UI Review on/off, clash handling, etc., each with on/off and settings), Auto-lander (status, last runs, what's waiting and why, land now / pause), and History. Per the final layout: the screens live in the console only; the rules and lander logic run in the axf-molly container; axHub only routes the gate.* and lander.* tools. Until axf-molly exists, read/write through the current orchestrator/lander code. Coordinate with auto-lander-controls-in-the-gate-plugin and move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub. Rows follow the skin's 1-or-2-row grid setting. Full API parity, tests, help, Shipped features. Land when done.

Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

after.title: axf-molly container: orchestrator, gate, lander, Shipped sender
after.detail: Replaces move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub (its 37 steps were planned for the old axHub-screens layout and its s1 gate waits on a precondition that no longer applies). FINAL LAYOUT (Brett): console = screens only; axf-molly = does all the work; axHub = routes + credentials/approvals only, no screens, no data; axf-data = stores all data. BUILD a private container 'axf-molly' on Coolify (no public port/DNS, internal Docker network, auto-restart). Check the name doesn't clash with the old standalone Molly app (it's retired; list any leftover container/cron/domain for retirement, delete nothing without listing it). MOVE INTO IT: orchestrator, dispatcher/pipeline tick, reconciler, splitter, slots/accounts routing, gate rules engine (framework/core/gate-rules.mjs from gate-rules-plugin-in-the-console), auto-lander + merge queue with the 'Merge queue on/off' switch, and the merge watch / Shipped features sender (vps-sends-shipped-features-every-merge). It reads/writes ALL data through axf-data (data-container-axf-data-holds-all, data-store@1 client), never repo files. HOST ACCESS: a narrow host bridge (mounted /root/axf-builds worktrees, git, claude CLI, tmux runner) to launch and watch build sessions; NOT the Docker socket; document exactly what it can touch. axHub registers axf-molly as a downstream and exposes orchestrator.*, gate.*, lander.*, features.* tools (equivalents for axf-console.build_orchestrator_pipeline_request and planner.builds). Console orchestrator, Gate & rules and Shipped features screens talk to it through axHub. STAGING: shadow first (axf-molly computes, console acts, diff log), then cutover with an owner lease and undo; builds keep running during the switch; no build or history lost. FIX ON THE WAY: phase-end builds must never be parked in Pending (reconciler bug); dispatcher alert links use view:build-orchestrator. Console-down drill: stop the console and prove builds still launch, land and get Shipped features. Order: start right after axf-data is up (its API and client exist on PR #704). Tests, help, Shipped features. Land each part with the one-at-a-time lander.

origin.said: Yes do those containers and wire them and migrate everything asap. Molly's gonna run the orchestrator from now on, so let's name it AXF Molly.

before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

axf-data tests: pytest for CRUD, rev conflicts, journal append-only, restore and auth refusal

Console server data layer: a Python data-store client (apps/console-web/server/data_store.py) that honours the mode (local/shadow/cutover) and exposes the same functions the server uses today for _data and plugin dataDirs
Route persist.mjs and the plugin data helpers through framework/core/data-store.mjs (local backend by default, axf-data when the mode says so). No behaviour change in local mode

Settings, planner items and UI Review on data-store: switch the claude-settings, plan-studio and ui-review storage calls to the client
Notes, changes log and SQLite ledgers (shipped-features, others) on data-store: blob or table namespaces through the client

Migration tool framework/cli/data-migrate.mjs: plan (counts per namespace), backup first (required), copy, then verify counts and hashes against the manifest. Refuse to finish on any mismatch. Dry-run by default

Shadow mode wiring: framework/cli/data-mode.mjs status|shadow|cutover|rollback (cutover refused unless shadow has run with zero drift for the set window), with the diff log written to axf-data

Console UI: Settings → Plugins → Data store sub-tab (mode, namespaces with counts, last backup, drift log, Backup now / Verify / Shadow / Cut over / Roll back with confirm) built from framework controls and tokens only, with data-axf-target addresses

before.title: Data container: axf-data holds all console data
before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

steps.text: Design the modes switch (local → shadow → cutover → rollback): in shadow, writes go to local and to axf-data, reads come from local, and a diff log records any drift. steps.why: Changes how every app persists data; a cross-app behaviour contract

steps.text: Contract checks: framework/spec/check-data-store.mjs runs the client against the fixtures for rev conflicts, journal append-only, mode transitions and count manifests. Wire it into CI

axf-data tests: pytest for CRUD, rev conflicts, journal append-only, restore and auth refusal

Console server data layer: a Python data-store client (apps/console-web/server/data_store.py) that honours the mode (local/shadow/cutover) and exposes the same functions the server uses today for _data and plugin dataDirs
Route persist.mjs and the plugin data helpers through framework/core/data-store.mjs (local backend by default, axf-data when the mode says so). No behaviour change in local mode

Notes, changes log and SQLite ledgers (shipped-features, others) on data-store: blob or table namespaces through the client

after.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Data container: axf-data holds all console data
before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Data container: axf-data holds all console data
before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Data container: axf-data holds all console data
before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

steps.text: Design the modes switch (local → shadow → cutover → rollback): in shadow, writes go to local and to axf-data, reads come from local, and a diff log records any drift. steps.why: Changes how every app persists data; a cross-app behaviour contract

steps.text: Contract checks: framework/spec/check-data-store.mjs runs the client against the fixtures for rev conflicts, journal append-only, mode transitions and count manifests. Wire it into CI

axf-data tests: pytest for CRUD, rev conflicts, journal append-only, restore and auth refusal

Console server data layer: a Python data-store client (apps/console-web/server/data_store.py) that honours the mode (local/shadow/cutover) and exposes the same functions the server uses today for _data and plugin dataDirs
Route persist.mjs and the plugin data helpers through framework/core/data-store.mjs (local backend by default, axf-data when the mode says so). No behaviour change in local mode

Notes, changes log and SQLite ledgers (shipped-features, others) on data-store: blob or table namespaces through the client

after.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.title: Move build orchestrator to axHub
before.detail: Move the entire build orchestrator (queue, pending, splitter, dispatcher/pipeline tick, reconciler, slots, accounts, builds store, notes, steps, landing) out of the console plugin and into axHub (MossesX/axHub), running on the VPS, so builds are managed whether the console is up or not. Staged so nothing breaks mid-flight: (1) Run AFTER auto-lander-controls-in-the-gate-plugin lands (gate + merge queue already in axHub). (2) Stand up the axHub orchestrator service reading the SAME builds store (_claude/builds/*), in shadow mode: it computes what it would launch/land but doesn't act; compare with the console for a while. (3) Cut over: axHub owns the dispatcher, reconciler, splitter and lander; the console's cron/plugin stops acting. (4) Build the full orchestrator UI as axHub screens (all tabs: Pending, Queue, Active, Built, Complete, Errors, Archive, settings, slots, accounts) with every action. (5) axHub tools (orchestrator.*) for Claude, MCP and voice: file a build, note, status, step, approve, land, etc.; today's axf-console.build_orchestrator_pipeline_request and planner.builds callers get equivalent axHub tools. (6) Console keeps only a read-only mirror or a link to the axHub page, then the console plugin is retired. Fix on the way: phase-end builds must never get parked in Pending (reconciler bug), dispatcher alerts link format. No build or data lost; all history migrated. Tests, help, Shipped features.

The container needs controlled host access to launch/watch builds (tmux sessions, /root/axf-builds worktrees, git, claude CLI, the builds store): use a narrow host bridge (mounted paths + a small host-side runner/agent), not a wide-open docker socket; document exactly what it can touch. before.title: Data container: axf-data holds all console data
before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

steps.text: Design the migration and its count checks: list every data source the console writes today (/projects/*/_data, _claude/builds, plugin lifecycle.dataDir, SQLite ledgers, settings), map each to a namespace, and define the per-namespace count+hash manifest and the rollback rule. Write framework/spec/fixtures/data-store-migration.json and the DATA-STORE.md migration section
steps.why: Schema + migration design; nothing may be lost

steps.text: Design the modes switch (local → shadow → cutover → rollback): in shadow, writes go to local and to axf-data, reads come from local, and a diff log records any drift. After cutover axf-data is the only store and local becomes the read-only backup. Write the mode state machine in framework/core/data-store-mode.mjs with a fixture
steps.why: Changes how every app persists data; a cross-app behaviour contract

steps.text: Contract checks: framework/spec/check-data-store.mjs runs the client against the fixtures for rev conflicts, journal append-only, mode transitions and count manifests. Wire it into CI
Scaffold the axf-data service: services/axf-data/ (FastAPI, SQLite + blob dir on a Docker volume, /health), data-store@1 routes get/put/list/append/snapshot with rev checks, and token auth
axf-data journal and history: append-only journal tables, per-record history with restore(rev), and a watch endpoint (SSE) for change feeds
axf-data tests: pytest for CRUD, rev conflicts, journal append-only, restore and auth refusal

Dockerfile and Coolify deploy for axf-data: private app, no public port or domain, internal network only, restart unless-stopped, named volume. Add a deploy/install-data.sh helper using framework/deploy/axf-deploy.sh, and log the deploy with axf_deploy_log

Daily backups: an axf-data snapshot job (tar of the SQLite online backup + blobs, keep 14 days plus weekly copies) to /root/hub/data/axf-data/backups, with a restore command and a verify step that checks counts against the live store
Backup health check: register an axf.health@1 check in systems-check (last backup age, verify result, axf-data reachable) with Auto fix to run a backup or restart the container

Console server data layer: a Python data-store client (apps/console-web/server/data_store.py) that honours the mode (local/shadow/cutover) and exposes the same functions the server uses today for _data and plugin dataDirs
Route persist.mjs and the plugin data helpers through framework/core/data-store.mjs (local backend by default, axf-data when the mode says so). No behaviour change in local mode

Builds store on data-store: framework/cli/builds-store.mjs reads and writes store, journal and history through the client (lock = rev check), so axf-molly can use it too. Coordinate with move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub and add a note on that build
Settings, planner items and UI Review on data-store: switch the claude-settings, plan-studio and ui-review storage calls to the client
Notes, changes log and SQLite ledgers (shipped-features, others) on data-store: blob or table namespaces through the client

Migration tool framework/cli/data-migrate.mjs: plan (counts per namespace), backup first (required), copy, then verify counts and hashes against the manifest. Refuse to finish on any mismatch. Dry-run by default
Migration tests on a seeded copy of real data: migrate, verify, roll back, re-run idempotently, and a forced mismatch must fail
Shadow mode wiring: framework/cli/data-mode.mjs status|shadow|cutover|rollback (cutover refused unless shadow has run with zero drift for the set window), with the diff log written to axf-data

Console UI: Settings → Plugins → Data store sub-tab (mode, namespaces with counts, last backup, drift log, Backup now / Verify / Shadow / Cut over / Roll back with confirm) built from framework controls and tokens only, with data-axf-target addresses

Data store API parity: REST routes /api/plugins/data-store/{state,backup,verify,mode}, plugin commands (MCP), axf CLI (axf data …), voice actions, console_show deep link view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins/data-store, and console-control targets
Plugin lifecycle for data-store: install.mjs and uninstall.mjs (data stays in axf-data), help entry, glossary descriptions, notify.json for backup and drift alerts

axHub route only: register axf-data as an axHub downstream (routes plus the service token kept in axHub; no data stored in axHub) so notes, builds and settings tools work when the console is down. Document the tools in the README

Console-down drill: a script that stops the console container in a test compose, then checks that axf-data answers through the axHub route and that a builds-store write from the axf-molly side lands. Record the result
UI Review: submit 3 options for the Data store tab (choices as settings assets in plugins/data-store/assets/settings/), with desktop and phone shots

Shipped features and docs: add a feature-ledger row for each piece, update CLAUDE.md layout/conventions (four-part layout), _claude/memory/decisions.md and STATUS.md, then catalog/status.json and tracker.mjs

Tests, report and PR: run check-data-store, check-data-migrate, the axf-data pytest, check-theme/controls/console-control/toolbars, plugin-lifecycle check and the glossary check. Write _claude/builds/reports/data-container-axf-data-holds-all.md (cutover is staged: shadow first, then cutover once drift is zero), add the THREADS row, open the PR describing how each part is reached by REST, MCP, CLI and voice, and link it with builds-live

before.title: axf-molly container: orchestrator, gate, lander, Shipped sender
before.detail: Replaces move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub (its 37 steps were planned for the old axHub-screens layout and its s1 gate waits on a precondition that no longer applies). FINAL LAYOUT (Brett): console = screens only; axf-molly = does all the work; axHub = routes + credentials/approvals only, no screens, no data; axf-data = stores all data. BUILD a private container 'axf-molly' on Coolify (no public port/DNS, internal Docker network, auto-restart). Check the name doesn't clash with the old standalone Molly app (it's retired; list any leftover container/cron/domain for retirement, delete nothing without listing it). MOVE INTO IT: orchestrator, dispatcher/pipeline tick, reconciler, splitter, slots/accounts routing, gate rules engine (framework/core/gate-rules.mjs from gate-rules-plugin-in-the-console), auto-lander + merge queue with the 'Merge queue on/off' switch, and the merge watch / Shipped features sender (vps-sends-shipped-features-every-merge). It reads/writes ALL data through axf-data (data-container-axf-data-holds-all, data-store@1 client), never repo files. HOST ACCESS: a narrow host bridge (mounted /root/axf-builds worktrees, git, claude CLI, tmux runner) to launch and watch build sessions; NOT the Docker socket; document exactly what it can touch. axHub registers axf-molly as a downstream and exposes orchestrator.*, gate.*, lander.*, features.* tools (equivalents for axf-console.build_orchestrator_pipeline_request and planner.builds). Console orchestrator, Gate & rules and Shipped features screens talk to it through axHub. STAGING: shadow first (axf-molly computes, console acts, diff log), then cutover with an owner lease and undo; builds keep running during the switch; no build or history lost. FIX ON THE WAY: phase-end builds must never be parked in Pending (reconciler bug); dispatcher alert links use view:build-orchestrator. Console-down drill: stop the console and prove builds still launch, land and get Shipped features. Order: start right after axf-data is up (its API and client exist on PR #704). Tests, help, Shipped features. Land each part with the one-at-a-time lander.

before.title: Data container: axf-data holds all console data
before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

before.detail: Brett's final layout: the console is screens ONLY, with no work and no data in it. New private container 'axf-data' (Coolify, auto-restart, no public port or DNS, internal Docker network only) holds ALL the data: notes, builds store/journal/history, settings, planner items, UI reviews, everything the console stores today. Four parts: console = UI only; axf-molly = does the work (orchestrator, gate, lander); axHub = routes plus credentials/keys only (NO app data stored in axHub); axf-data = stores everything. Goal: if the console goes down, all data and notes stay available (through axHub tools) and builds keep running. Stage it safely: an API in front of the store, migrate with count checks and a backup, run in shadow first, then cut over, and no data is ever lost. Add daily backups. Coordinate with the move-build-orchestrator-to-axhub build (axf-molly reads and writes the builds store through axf-data). Tests, help, Shipped features.

split.note: Split by Claude into 16 steps (4 Fable).

steps.text: Design the home-cards@1 contract: a pure resolver (picks + enabled plugins + activity scores + slot count -> ordered cards marked pinned/auto) and the plugin-activity@1 score record (opens, actions, live jobs, alerts, decay window). Write the schema and an INTEROP/PORTING note marking the Android twin as a deferred gap.
steps.why: New cross-app contract and schema that decides how the home screen GUI fills

steps.text: Build the reference engine framework/core/engines/home-cards.mjs: drop disabled or uninstalled plugins, keep Brett's pins in his order, fill free slots with the top-ranked enabled plugins (stable tie-break by id), never leave a gap, and cap at the slot count.
steps.why: Engine internals of the new contract

steps.text: Build the activity ranking engine: score = weighted opens/actions/live jobs/alerts with time decay over the window. Turn a raw event log into ranked plugin ids.
steps.why: Engine internals: ranking rules other apps will reuse

steps.text: Write golden fixtures and a checker: disable removes the card and the next-ranked plugin takes its place, re-enable brings it back, an empty selection still fills every slot, pins keep their order, slot count changes.
steps.why: Conformance fixtures for the new contract

steps.text: Find the console home screen and its card store. Add the slot-count setting (axf.home.slots, default 6, levelled) and the stored picks list {pinned ids in order, removed ids}, migrating today's selection into pins.

before.title: Home cards follow plugin on/off; home always filled with most-active plugins
before.detail: 1) When a plugin is disabled or uninstalled, its home screen card is removed at once (no dead or blank cards), and comes back if the plugin is re-enabled. 2) The home screen is never empty or gappy: empty slots are filled automatically. 3) Brett's own picks always win and keep their order. Any slot he hasn't picked is filled with the MOST ACTIVE enabled plugins, ranked by recent use and activity (opens, actions, live jobs, alerts over a recent window). The ranking updates over time and auto-filled cards are marked as auto (pin to keep, remove to swap). 4) Setting for number of home slots; cards use the shared skin row/card styling. Full API parity (list home cards, pin/unpin, reorder, refill, ranking) via REST/MCP/CLI/voice. Tests (disable plugin removes its card and a replacement fills in; empty selection still fills the home screen), help, Shipped features. Land with the one-at-a-time lander.

UI Review: take desktop and phone shots of the home screen and settings with 3 option assets (card density/layout) via review.mjs submit --choices.

before.title: Build rules tab in Gate & rules: VPS owns and enforces all builder rules
before.detail: Add a Build rules tab to the Gate & rules plugin (PR #711), with the VPS as the ONE owner and enforcer of every builder rule. 1) Inventory ALL builder rules in CLAUDE.md, the build briefs, the dispatcher prompt templates (Look/API/Checkpoints/Rules blocks), and the _claude rule docs. VPS fixers 3: API-parity scaffolding (plugin-commands route + MCP + CLI + voice action stubs for a new plugin setting or action) and tracker/THREADS rows (tracker.mjs regen + THREADS Live line), in apps/console-web/plugins/gate-rules/fixers/.

VPS fixers 4: run-ci-checks (runs each rule's check command in agent-slots heavy, collects pass/fail) and pr-open-link (opens the PR through github-token.mjs, then builds-live.mjs link) in apps/console-web/plugins/gate-rules/fixers/.

Rule runner: apps/console-web/plugins/gate-rules/build-rules-runner.mjs runs the enabled VPS rules for a build at a phase (before|after|gate), calls each check, runs the autofix on a fail, re-checks, and writes every result to the rule history and gate History.

Dispatcher wiring: pipeline.mjs runs the 'before' VPS rules before launch and builds the session brief's Look/API/Checkpoints/Rules blocks from briefBlocks(store) instead of hardcoded text; the build's end hook runs the 'after' VPS rules.

Gate wiring: landing-line/gate-rules verdict evaluates every enabled build rule (phase gate) before landing; a fail blocks, the runner auto-fixes what it can, re-checks, and logs to History; unfixable ones raise a systems-check banner item.

Server REST: /api/plugins/gate-rules/build-rules list/get/add/edit/toggle/delete(confirm)/history/run (dry-run and real), using framework/core/build-rules.mjs; deciding nothing personOnly is needed here, destructive delete needs confirm.

API parity for the backend: gate.build_rules_* MCP tools via plugin-commands, CLI apps/console-web/plugins/gate-rules/build-rules.mjs (list|get|add|edit|on|off|history|run), voice actions build-rules.list/toggle/add/run, all four calling the same REST.
UI: a Build rules tab in the Gate & rules plugin (TabGroup on the tab-group asset): DataGrid of rules with doer, kind, phase, on/off Switch and last result; framework controls and tokens only.
UI: add/edit rule dialog (dialog asset, TextField/SelectField for doer, kind, phase, check, autofix, brief block) and a History panel per rule; toolbar with role=toolbar + aria-label.

API parity for the UI: console-control addresses (view:gate-rules/tab:build-rules, row:<rule>, setting:<rule>.enabled) via data-axf-target, console_show deep links for the tab, a rule and its history, state readable through console_control_get.

Seed the live store: run the migration into /projects/amberx-axf/_data/build-rules/ (persist.mjs data.shared entry in project.manifest.json) and make sure the runner reads it there with the repo seed as fallback.

# Build: home-cards-follow-plugin-off-home-always

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-15T13:22:11.842Z
> When I disable plugins, the home cards need to be disabled as well. They need to be removed, and other ones need to replace them. The home screen always needs to be filled with some plugins, even if I don't have some selected. Yes, I can select which ones I want, but if I don't, you need to pick some. Pick the most active.

## What to build

The home screen always needs to be filled with some plugins, even if I don't have some selected. Yes, I can select which ones I want, but if I don't, you need to pick some. Pick the most active."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

Write the schema and an INTEROP/PORTING note marking the Android twin as a deferred gap.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Build the reference engine framework/core/engines/home-cards.mjs: drop disabled or uninstalled plugins, keep Brett's pins in his order, fill free slots with the top-ranked enabled plugins (stable tie-break by id), never leave a gap, and cap at the slot count.
[ ] s3 (~10 min) Build the activity ranking engine: score = weighted opens/actions/live jobs/alerts with time decay over the window. Turn a raw event log into ranked plugin ids.
[ ] s4 (~10 min) Write golden fixtures and a checker: disable removes the card and the next-ranked plugin takes its place, re-enable brings it back, an empty selection still fills every slot, pins keep their order, slot count changes.
Read first: framework/schemas/home-cards.json, framework/spec/PORTING.md, framework/spec/HOME-CARDS.md, framework/core/engines/home-cards.mjs, framework/core/engines/plugin-activity.mjs, framework/spec/fixtures/home-cards.json, framework/spec/check-home-cards.mjs

steps.text: Write the phone-connect@1 contract: the device record, pairing handshake, hub sign-in and session security rules (carried over from AmberX), command envelope (open_url, notify, approvals watch, recorder start/stop/status) and wire error codes. Spec doc plus JSON schema.
steps.why: New cross-app protocol contract between the console, axHub and the Android companion

steps.text: Write the reference core for the contract: validators for the device record and command envelope, and the pairing state machine (unpaired → pending → paired → revoked). Add golden fixtures.
steps.why: Engine internals + conformance fixtures the Android app and server both follow

steps.text: Design the migration: amberx.open_url → phone.open_url and amberx.recorder_* → phone.recorder_* aliases (alias table + deprecation note), output-recorder data dir → phone-connect data dir, and the axHub amberx device record → a phone-connect device. Write the migration script with a dry run.
steps.why: Schema + data migration design across console, axHub tools and stored recordings

steps.text: Inventory before anything is deleted: list every apps/amberx-droid piece (pages, services, Capacitor shell, wake word, voice, notes, dictation, web tabs, AI connection, assistant, agent manager, walkthrough recorder), every console plugin being removed or moved (wake-listener, output-recorder) and the deploy (amberx.amberxai.com) and axHub amberx device. Mark each as kept and ported, merged into the console AI Assistant, or dropped. Commit it as the removal list.

Scaffold the phone-connect console plugin: plugin.json (builtWith Opus, description, lifecycle dataDir, uiEditor none), install.mjs and uninstall.mjs, a README and a notify.json declaring the FYI, fix-update, alert and approval notification types.

Build the server device registry and pairing routes on the core: pair code issue/claim, device list/get/revoke, heartbeat/online state. Uses the hub session for sign-in, and only Brett's own session can approve a pairing (personOnly).

Add server command routes: open_url (amberxai.com https only, Chrome or the default browser) and notify (FYI, fix updates, alerts through axf.notify@1). Queue commands for the device, with delivery acks.

Move the whole output recorder out of the output-recorder plugin into phone-connect: session start/stop/status, 30-minute parts, the upload intake to axHub groups, the transcription hook and the opt-in mic switch. Keep the straight-approval rule on start.
Finish the recorder move: point claude-session's automatic recording at phone-connect through a capability (axf.phone-recorder@1), not a folder name, and run the data migration for existing parts.
Add auto-approval rules on the server: rule store (what, scope, expiry), evaluated for the Monitor watch, never covering destructive tools or personOnly actions. Routes to list, add and remove rules.

Expose MCP tools through plugin-commands: phone_devices, phone_pair, phone_revoke, phone_open_url, phone_notify, phone_recorder_start/stop/status, phone_rules_*. Register the amberx_* aliases from the alias table.

Add axHub-side tools: phone.open_url, phone.recorder_start/stop/status, with amberx.* kept as aliases (same policies: recorder_start is a straight approval). Do it as a veto-call PR on MossesX/axHub, or record it as a follow-up item if this checkout can't reach axHub.
Add the CLI: axf phone devices|pair|revoke|open|notify|recorder start/stop/status|rules list/add/remove, all on the same REST routes.

Build the console UI, a Settings → Plugins → Phone Connect sub-tab: device card (online, last seen), pair with QR/code, revoke, notification switches per type, and the level toolbar. Framework controls and tokens only, TabGroup for the tabs.
Build console screens: Recorder (on/off, current part, uploaded parts, queue, start/stop) and Auto-approval rules (list, add, remove), in framework controls only.

API for the UI: console-control targets (data-axf-target) for every screen, tab, setting and button. console_show deep links (view:phone-connect/…), state reads, and voice actions phone.open / phone.notify / phone.recorder.* / phone.pair in the console actions registry.

Create the Android companion app: apps/phone-connect-droid with project.manifest.json, a Gradle app module (ai.amberx.axf.phoneconnect, API 35) and an Axf-themed Compose shell with three tabs (Approvals, Monitor, Settings). This is native and small, not the console.
Android: port hub sign-in and session security from amberx-droid (hub session storage, token refresh, sign-out, pairing claim screen) onto the phone-connect@1 pairing flow.

Android: port the Approvals page (list, detail with reason title/description, Approve / Deny / Shelve with Brett's own hub session) and alerts. The lock screen shows only 'Approval waiting' (VISIBILITY_SECRET content plus a public version).
Android: port Monitor as the WatchService foreground service: approvals watch, alerts, auto-approval rule evaluation (rules synced from the server), and a persistent low-priority notification.

Android: command channel plus open page. Receive phone-connect@1 commands, then for open_url (amberxai.com https only) bring Chrome or the default browser to the front, with a high-priority tap-to-open notification fallback when a background start is blocked. Ack each delivery.
Android: phone notifications. Channels for FYI, fix updates, alerts and approvals, matching notify.json, with per-type switches synced from the console settings.

Android: move the whole Audio Output Recorder in from amberx-droid. MediaProjection playback capture (mic only with the opt-in switch), 30-minute parts named '<session> - <date> - partN', an upload queue to axHub groups, and status reports.

Android: Settings tab (paired console, sign-out, notification switches, recorder mic opt-in, Monitor on/off) with Axf controls only. Every setting is also settable from the console API through the command channel.

CI: build the Phone Connect APK in .github/workflows/android.yml (artifact phone-connect-debug.apk), add the app to conform checks and the shared-assets list if needed, and update the Android-on-hold exception to name Phone Connect in place of AmberX.
Merge AmberX's phone AI assistant and agent manager into the console AI Assistant: carry over anything it has that the console assistant lacks (per the inventory), or note it as covered.

Remove the console wake-listener plugin and the always-on wake mic: run uninstall.mjs --all, delete the folder and its lifecycle-marked doc lines, pass plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall, and shift the help ratchet.
Remove the emptied output-recorder plugin (uninstall.mjs --all, lifecycle check), leaving only the aliases in phone-connect.

Tests: Python tests for pairing, commands, recorder, rules and aliases; check-phone-connect fixtures; console-control and toolbar/theme/chrome checks on the new UI; a Kotlin unit test for lock-screen visibility and URL filtering.
Help, Shipped features and glossary: help pages for Phone Connect (console and phone), each feature described at its definition, a deploy-log line, and catalog --check passing.

UI Review: submit console desktop and phone shots plus Android screens with at least 3 options each as assets (settings interface takes one). Ask Brett for the group name, or use the build-id group when headless.

Retirement gate script: verify Phone Connect is installed and working (device paired, heartbeat online, a test notify acked, open_url acked, recorder status answers). Retirement below runs only if it passes, otherwise it is recorded as waiting on Brett's phone.

Retire AmberX after the gate: delete apps/amberx-droid and its manifest, drop it from shared-assets, the rules and the CI APK job, and remove the amberx.amberxai.com deploy (Coolify app and DNS record logged in the DNS log) and the axHub amberx device as veto calls with reasons. before.title: Phone Connect: small Android companion + console plugin; retire AmberX
before.detail: Replace the AmberX app with Phone Connect. Two parts: (A) a console plugin 'phone-connect' for screens, settings and pairing, with full API parity; (B) a SMALL native Android companion app, not the whole console, for phone-only work. KEEP and port from apps/amberx-droid: 1) the Approvals page with alerts, including the lock screen showing only 'Approval waiting'; 2) Monitor: background WatchService foreground service, approvals watch, alerts, auto-approval rules; 3) open a page on the phone (bring Chrome to the front; keep the amberx.open_url tool working in axHub, renamed phone.open_url with an alias); 4) phone notifications (FYI and fix updates, alerts); 5) the audio output recorder: move the WHOLE thing out of the console's output-recorder plugin into Phone Connect (recorder_start/stop/status tools move too, with aliases). DROP: voice commands, notes, dictation, web tabs, AI connection, the phone AI assistant and agent manager (everything merges into the console AI Assistant), the walkthrough video and recorder, and the wake word listener. Also REMOVE the console wake-listener plugin and the always-on wake mic, because it grabs Brett's mic. Keep the hub sign-in and session security rules. Before deleting anything, list every AmberX piece and console plugin being removed, then retire apps/amberx-droid, the amberx.amberxai.com deploy, and the axHub amberx device, once Phone Connect is installed and working. CI builds the APK. Tests, help, Shipped features. Land with the one-at-a-time lander.

notes.text: Queued by console.

Brett (08:37): the phone app has NO screens of its own. It is a background service plus a one-time sign-in/permissions page only. Approvals, Monitor rules, recorder controls and all settings live in the console plugin; tapping a notification opens the matching console page in the browser.

Brett (08:38): CORRECTION, the phone app DOES show things on screen as an OVERLAY. Fold in the floating always-on-top toolbar overlay from build amberx-floating-toolbar-always-on-top-mic-approvals-build-status (approvals, build status, notifications widget). Approvals and alerts pop up right on the phone screen over other apps, and he can approve from the overlay. Settings still live in the console. List what that old build already did before porting it.

Brett (08:39): the overlay toolbar collapses to a small floating button (draggable, remembers its spot and its collapsed/expanded state); tap to expand, tap to collapse. A new approval or alert pops up from the button even while it's collapsed, with a badge count.

Brett (08:40): lots of overlay settings, all in the console plugin and synced to the phone. Settings for each popup type (approvals, alerts, notifications): where it appears (top, bottom, center, corners, from the button), entry/exit animation (slide down from top, burst out from the middle, circle/radial reveal, fade, scale, bounce), speed, size, how long it stays, sound/vibrate, and opacity. Settings for the toolbar and button: size, shape, edge snapping, and auto-collapse delay. Live preview in the console, presets, and full API parity.

Brett (08:41): the overlay, button, toolbar and popups are themed by the console's current skin and theme (same tokens through Axf.colors/type/space/shapes on Android). When he changes the skin or theme in the console, the phone overlay updates live without a new APK.
Split by Claude into 34 steps (3 Fable).

origin.said: We're gonna build phone connect. Plug in, and it's gonna contain these features. Approval page, add it. Monitor yes. Voice commands get rid of it, it's buggy. Notes, dictation, web tabs, AI connection gone. AI assistant and agent manager kill it, merge everything into the assistant in the console. Walkthrough video kill it. Open pages on phone keep it. Notifications keep it. Audio recorder, remove it out of console and put the whole thing in the phone app. Wake word listener kill it. Do we need a whole console app?

split.note: Split by Claude into 34 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Write the phone-connect@1 contract: the device record, pairing handshake, hub sign-in and session security rules (carried over from AmberX), command envelope (open_url, notify, approvals watch, recorder start/stop/status) and wire error codes. Spec doc plus JSON schema.
steps.why: New cross-app protocol contract between the console, axHub and the Android companion

steps.text: Write the reference core for the contract: validators for the device record and command envelope, and the pairing state machine (unpaired → pending → paired → revoked). Add golden fixtures.
steps.why: Engine internals + conformance fixtures the Android app and server both follow

steps.text: Design the migration: amberx.open_url → phone.open_url and amberx.recorder_* → phone.recorder_* aliases (alias table + deprecation note), output-recorder data dir → phone-connect data dir, and the axHub amberx device record → a phone-connect device. Write the migration script with a dry run.
steps.why: Schema + data migration design across console, axHub tools and stored recordings

steps.text: Inventory before anything is deleted: list every apps/amberx-droid piece (pages, services, Capacitor shell, wake word, voice, notes, dictation, web tabs, AI connection, assistant, agent manager, walkthrough recorder), every console plugin being removed or moved (wake-listener, output-recorder) and the deploy (amberx.amberxai.com) and axHub amberx device. Mark each as kept and ported, merged into the console AI Assistant, or dropped. Commit it as the removal list.

Scaffold the phone-connect console plugin: plugin.json (builtWith Opus, description, lifecycle dataDir, uiEditor none), install.mjs and uninstall.mjs, a README and a notify.json declaring the FYI, fix-update, alert and approval notification types.

Build the server device registry and pairing routes on the core: pair code issue/claim, device list/get/revoke, heartbeat/online state. Uses the hub session for sign-in, and only Brett's own session can approve a pairing (personOnly).

Add server command routes: open_url (amberxai.com https only, Chrome or the default browser) and notify (FYI, fix updates, alerts through axf.notify@1). Queue commands for the device, with delivery acks.

Move the whole output recorder out of the output-recorder plugin into phone-connect: session start/stop/status, 30-minute parts, the upload intake to axHub groups, the transcription hook and the opt-in mic switch. Keep the straight-approval rule on start.
Finish the recorder move: point claude-session's automatic recording at phone-connect through a capability (axf.phone-recorder@1), not a folder name, and run the data migration for existing parts.
Add auto-approval rules on the server: rule store (what, scope, expiry), evaluated for the Monitor watch, never covering destructive tools or personOnly actions. Routes to list, add and remove rules.

Expose MCP tools through plugin-commands: phone_devices, phone_pair, phone_revoke, phone_open_url, phone_notify, phone_recorder_start/stop/status, phone_rules_*. Register the amberx_* aliases from the alias table.

Add axHub-side tools: phone.open_url, phone.recorder_start/stop/status, with amberx.* kept as aliases (same policies: recorder_start is a straight approval). Do it as a veto-call PR on MossesX/axHub, or record it as a follow-up item if this checkout can't reach axHub.
Add the CLI: axf phone devices|pair|revoke|open|notify|recorder start/stop/status|rules list/add/remove, all on the same REST routes.

Build the console UI, a Settings → Plugins → Phone Connect sub-tab: device card (online, last seen), pair with QR/code, revoke, notification switches per type, and the level toolbar. Framework controls and tokens only, TabGroup for the tabs.
Build console screens: Recorder (on/off, current part, uploaded parts, queue, start/stop) and Auto-approval rules (list, add, remove), in framework controls only.

API for the UI: console-control targets (data-axf-target) for every screen, tab, setting and button. console_show deep links (view:phone-connect/…), state reads, and voice actions phone.open / phone.notify / phone.recorder.* / phone.pair in the console actions registry.

Create the Android companion app: apps/phone-connect-droid with project.manifest.json, a Gradle app module (ai.amberx.axf.phoneconnect, API 35) and an Axf-themed Compose shell with three tabs (Approvals, Monitor, Settings). This is native and small, not the console.
Android: port hub sign-in and session security from amberx-droid (hub session storage, token refresh, sign-out, pairing claim screen) onto the phone-connect@1 pairing flow.

Android: port the Approvals page (list, detail with reason title/description, Approve / Deny / Shelve with Brett's own hub session) and alerts. The lock screen shows only 'Approval waiting' (VISIBILITY_SECRET content plus a public version).
Android: port Monitor as the WatchService foreground service: approvals watch, alerts, auto-approval rule evaluation (rules synced from the server), and a persistent low-priority notification.

Android: command channel plus open page. Receive phone-connect@1 commands, then for open_url (amberxai.com https only) bring Chrome or the default browser to the front, with a high-priority tap-to-open notification fallback when a background start is blocked. Ack each delivery.
Android: phone notifications. Channels for FYI, fix updates, alerts and approvals, matching notify.json, with per-type switches synced from the console settings.

Android: move the whole Audio Output Recorder in from amberx-droid. MediaProjection playback capture (mic only with the opt-in switch), 30-minute parts named '<session> - <date> - partN', an upload queue to axHub groups, and status reports.

Android: Settings tab (paired console, sign-out, notification switches, recorder mic opt-in, Monitor on/off) with Axf controls only. Every setting is also settable from the console API through the command channel.

CI: build the Phone Connect APK in .github/workflows/android.yml (artifact phone-connect-debug.apk), add the app to conform checks and the shared-assets list if needed, and update the Android-on-hold exception to name Phone Connect in place of AmberX.
Merge AmberX's phone AI assistant and agent manager into the console AI Assistant: carry over anything it has that the console assistant lacks (per the inventory), or note it as covered.

Remove the console wake-listener plugin and the always-on wake mic: run uninstall.mjs --all, delete the folder and its lifecycle-marked doc lines, pass plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall, and shift the help ratchet.
Remove the emptied output-recorder plugin (uninstall.mjs --all, lifecycle check), leaving only the aliases in phone-connect.

Tests: Python tests for pairing, commands, recorder, rules and aliases; check-phone-connect fixtures; console-control and toolbar/theme/chrome checks on the new UI; a Kotlin unit test for lock-screen visibility and URL filtering.
Help, Shipped features and glossary: help pages for Phone Connect (console and phone), each feature described at its definition, a deploy-log line, and catalog --check passing.

Two parts: (A) a console plugin 'phone-connect' for screens, settings and pairing, with full API parity; (B) a SMALL native Android companion app, not the whole console, for phone-only work. KEEP and port from apps/amberx-droid: 1) the Approvals page with alerts, including the lock screen showing only 'Approval waiting'; 2) Monitor: background WatchService foreground service, approvals watch, alerts, auto-approval rules; 3) open a page on the phone (bring Chrome to the front; keep the amberx.open_url tool working in axHub, renamed phone.open_url with an alias); 4) phone notifications (FYI and fix updates, alerts); 5) the audio output recorder: move the WHOLE thing out of the console's output-recorder plugin into Phone Connect (recorder_start/stop/status tools move too, with aliases). DROP: voice commands, notes, dictation, web tabs, AI connection, the phone AI assistant and agent manager (everything merges into the console AI Assistant), the walkthrough video and recorder, and the wake word listener. Also REMOVE the console wake-listener plugin and the always-on wake mic, because it grabs Brett's mic. Keep the hub sign-in and session security rules. Before deleting anything, list every AmberX piece and console plugin being removed, then retire apps/amberx-droid, the amberx.amberxai.com deploy, and the axHub amberx device, once Phone Connect is installed and working. CI builds the APK. Tests, help, Shipped features. Land with the one-at-a-time lander.

Brett (08:38): CORRECTION, the phone app DOES show things on screen as an OVERLAY. Fold in the floating always-on-top toolbar overlay from build amberx-floating-toolbar-always-on-top-mic-approvals-build-status (approvals, build status, notifications widget). Approvals and alerts pop up right on the phone screen over other apps, and he can approve from the overlay. Settings still live in the console. List what that old build already did before porting it.

Brett (08:39): the overlay toolbar collapses to a small floating button (draggable, remembers its spot and its collapsed/expanded state); tap to expand, tap to collapse. A new approval or alert pops up from the button even while it's collapsed, with a badge count.

Brett (08:40): lots of overlay settings, all in the console plugin and synced to the phone. Settings for each popup type (approvals, alerts, notifications): where it appears (top, bottom, center, corners, from the button), entry/exit animation (slide down from top, burst out from the middle, circle/radial reveal, fade, scale, bounce), speed, size, how long it stays, sound/vibrate, and opacity. Settings for the toolbar and button: size, shape, edge snapping, and auto-collapse delay. Live preview in the console, presets, and full API parity.

Brett (08:41): the overlay, button, toolbar and popups are themed by the console's current skin and theme (same tokens through Axf.colors/type/space/shapes on Android). When he changes the skin or theme in the console, the phone overlay updates live without a new APK.

Write the migration script with a dry run.
Read first: framework/spec/PHONE-CONNECT.md, framework/schemas/phone-connect.json, framework/core/phone-connect.mjs, framework/spec/fixtures/phone-connect.json, framework/spec/check-phone-connect.mjs, apps/console-web/plugins/phone-connect/migrate.mjs

Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link phone-connect-small-android-companion --branch <b> --pr <n>.

Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step phone-connect-small-android-companion <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. split.note: Split by Claude into 34 steps (3 Fable).

steps.text: Write the phone-connect@1 contract: the device record, pairing handshake, hub sign-in and session security rules (carried over from AmberX), command envelope (open_url, notify, approvals watch, recorder start/stop/status) and wire error codes. Spec doc plus JSON schema.
steps.why: New cross-app protocol contract between the console, axHub and the Android companion

steps.text: Write the reference core for the contract: validators for the device record and command envelope, and the pairing state machine (unpaired → pending → paired → revoked). Add golden fixtures.
steps.why: Engine internals + conformance fixtures the Android app and server both follow

steps.text: Design the migration: amberx.open_url → phone.open_url and amberx.recorder_* → phone.recorder_* aliases (alias table + deprecation note), output-recorder data dir → phone-connect data dir, and the axHub amberx device record → a phone-connect device. Write the migration script with a dry run.
steps.why: Schema + data migration design across console, axHub tools and stored recordings

steps.text: Inventory before anything is deleted: list every apps/amberx-droid piece (pages, services, Capacitor shell, wake word, voice, notes, dictation, web tabs, AI connection, assistant, agent manager, walkthrough recorder), every console plugin being removed or moved (wake-listener, output-recorder) and the deploy (amberx.amberxai.com) and axHub amberx device. Mark each as kept and ported, merged into the console AI Assistant, or dropped. Commit it as the removal list.

Scaffold the phone-connect console plugin: plugin.json (builtWith Opus, description, lifecycle dataDir, uiEditor none), install.mjs and uninstall.mjs, a README and a notify.json declaring the FYI, fix-update, alert and approval notification types.

Build the server device registry and pairing routes on the core: pair code issue/claim, device list/get/revoke, heartbeat/online state. Uses the hub session for sign-in, and only Brett's own session can approve a pairing (personOnly).

Add server command routes: open_url (amberxai.com https only, Chrome or the default browser) and notify (FYI, fix updates, alerts through axf.notify@1). Queue commands for the device, with delivery acks.

Move the whole output recorder out of the output-recorder plugin into phone-connect: session start/stop/status, 30-minute parts, the upload intake to axHub groups, the transcription hook and the opt-in mic switch. Keep the straight-approval rule on start.
Finish the recorder move: point claude-session's automatic recording at phone-connect through a capability (axf.phone-recorder@1), not a folder name, and run the data migration for existing parts.
Add auto-approval rules on the server: rule store (what, scope, expiry), evaluated for the Monitor watch, never covering destructive tools or personOnly actions. Routes to list, add and remove rules.

Expose MCP tools through plugin-commands: phone_devices, phone_pair, phone_revoke, phone_open_url, phone_notify, phone_recorder_start/stop/status, phone_rules_*. Register the amberx_* aliases from the alias table.

Add axHub-side tools: phone.open_url, phone.recorder_start/stop/status, with amberx.* kept as aliases (same policies: recorder_start is a straight approval). Do it as a veto-call PR on MossesX/axHub, or record it as a follow-up item if this checkout can't reach axHub.
Add the CLI: axf phone devices|pair|revoke|open|notify|recorder start/stop/status|rules list/add/remove, all on the same REST routes.

Build the console UI, a Settings → Plugins → Phone Connect sub-tab: device card (online, last seen), pair with QR/code, revoke, notification switches per type, and the level toolbar. Framework controls and tokens only, TabGroup for the tabs.
Build console screens: Recorder (on/off, current part, uploaded parts, queue, start/stop) and Auto-approval rules (list, add, remove), in framework controls only.

API for the UI: console-control targets (data-axf-target) for every screen, tab, setting and button. console_show deep links (view:phone-connect/…), state reads, and voice actions phone.open / phone.notify / phone.recorder.* / phone.pair in the console actions registry.

Create the Android companion app: apps/phone-connect-droid with project.manifest.json, a Gradle app module (ai.amberx.axf.phoneconnect, API 35) and an Axf-themed Compose shell with three tabs (Approvals, Monitor, Settings). This is native and small, not the console.
Android: port hub sign-in and session security from amberx-droid (hub session storage, token refresh, sign-out, pairing claim screen) onto the phone-connect@1 pairing flow.

Android: port the Approvals page (list, detail with reason title/description, Approve / Deny / Shelve with Brett's own hub session) and alerts. The lock screen shows only 'Approval waiting' (VISIBILITY_SECRET content plus a public version).
Android: port Monitor as the WatchService foreground service: approvals watch, alerts, auto-approval rule evaluation (rules synced from the server), and a persistent low-priority notification.

Android: command channel plus open page. Receive phone-connect@1 commands, then for open_url (amberxai.com https only) bring Chrome or the default browser to the front, with a high-priority tap-to-open notification fallback when a background start is blocked. Ack each delivery.
Android: phone notifications. Channels for FYI, fix updates, alerts and approvals, matching notify.json, with per-type switches synced from the console settings.

Android: move the whole Audio Output Recorder in from amberx-droid. MediaProjection playback capture (mic only with the opt-in switch), 30-minute parts named '<session> - <date> - partN', an upload queue to axHub groups, and status reports.

Android: Settings tab (paired console, sign-out, notification switches, recorder mic opt-in, Monitor on/off) with Axf controls only. Every setting is also settable from the console API through the command channel.

CI: build the Phone Connect APK in .github/workflows/android.yml (artifact phone-connect-debug.apk), add the app to conform checks and the shared-assets list if needed, and update the Android-on-hold exception to name Phone Connect in place of AmberX.
Merge AmberX's phone AI assistant and agent manager into the console AI Assistant: carry over anything it has that the console assistant lacks (per the inventory), or note it as covered.

Remove the console wake-listener plugin and the always-on wake mic: run uninstall.mjs --all, delete the folder and its lifecycle-marked doc lines, pass plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall, and shift the help ratchet.
Remove the emptied output-recorder plugin (uninstall.mjs --all, lifecycle check), leaving only the aliases in phone-connect.

Tests: Python tests for pairing, commands, recorder, rules and aliases; check-phone-connect fixtures; console-control and toolbar/theme/chrome checks on the new UI; a Kotlin unit test for lock-screen visibility and URL filtering.
Help, Shipped features and glossary: help pages for Phone Connect (console and phone), each feature described at its definition, a deploy-log line, and catalog --check passing.

UI Review: submit console desktop and phone shots plus Android screens with at least 3 options each as assets (settings interface takes one). Ask Brett for the group name, or use the build-id group when headless.

Retirement gate script: verify Phone Connect is installed and working (device paired, heartbeat online, a test notify acked, open_url acked, recorder status answers). Retirement below runs only if it passes, otherwise it is recorded as waiting on Brett's phone.

Retire AmberX after the gate: delete apps/amberx-droid and its manifest, drop it from shared-assets, the rules and the CI APK job, and remove the amberx.amberxai.com deploy (Coolify app and DNS record logged in the DNS log) and the axHub amberx device as veto calls with reasons. Write a decision in memory/decisions.md.

Tests, report and landing: run the full check sweep, write _claude/builds/reports/phone-connect-small-android-companion.md (removal list, API reach for each feature: deep link / REST / MCP / CLI / voice, aliases, gaps), add the THREADS.md row, open the PR stating how each feature is reached and that UI Review is waiting, link it with builds-live, and land it with the one-at-a-time lander.

List every rule first and delete nothing without listing it. 2) Move them into a build-rules store on the VPS (later axf-data), served by REST and gate.* tools. 3) Each rule is marked doer = VPS or session. Mechanical rules are done by the VPS itself, before or after the build, and are removed from Claude's instructions so nothing happens twice. Examples: create the plugin home card from plugin.json and the template, the Shipped features manifest, the help stub, API-parity scaffolding, running the CI checks, tracker/THREADS rows, PR open and link, and landing one at a time. 4) Judgement rules (look and token rules, API parity design, step size) go into the session brief from the store at dispatch time and are not hardcoded in CLAUDE.md. 5) The gate checks every rule before landing; on a fail it blocks, the VPS auto-fixes what it can, and everything is logged in History. 6) The tab shows each rule with doer, on/off, edit, add, and history, with REST/MCP/CLI/voice parity. First rule: every plugin gets a home card, made by the VPS. Tests, help, Shipped features. Land with the one-at-a-time lander.

before.title: Phone Connect: small Android companion + console plugin; retire AmberX
before.detail: Replace the AmberX app with Phone Connect. Two parts: (A) a console plugin 'phone-connect' for screens, settings and pairing, with full API parity; (B) a SMALL native Android companion app, not the whole console, for phone-only work. KEEP and port from apps/amberx-droid: 1) the Approvals page with alerts, including the lock screen showing only 'Approval waiting'; 2) Monitor: background WatchService foreground service, approvals watch, alerts, auto-approval rules; 3) open a page on the phone (bring Chrome to the front; keep the amberx.open_url tool working in axHub, renamed phone.open_url with an alias); 4) phone notifications (FYI and fix updates, alerts); 5) the audio output recorder: move the WHOLE thing out of the console's output-recorder plugin into Phone Connect (recorder_start/stop/status tools move too, with aliases). DROP: voice commands, notes, dictation, web tabs, AI connection, the phone AI assistant and agent manager (everything merges into the console AI Assistant), the walkthrough video and recorder, and the wake word listener. Also REMOVE the console wake-listener plugin and the always-on wake mic, because it grabs Brett's mic. Keep the hub sign-in and session security rules. Before deleting anything, list every AmberX piece and console plugin being removed, then retire apps/amberx-droid, the amberx.amberxai.com deploy, and the axHub amberx device, once Phone Connect is installed and working. CI builds the APK. Tests, help, Shipped features. Land with the one-at-a-time lander.
